/// Custom Project For Browser Application To Build Maps for 2D games (Like La-Mulana) and take notes.

/// This was created as a pet project to test out "vibe coding" using Microsoft Copilot.

/// I am an experienced developer, but not an experienced front end designer, so this was fun.

/// Disclaimer - I did not review every line of code that was generated by AI.

File Structure:

-Maps

--[Application will generate map folders]

-global.json

-index.html

-server.js

-Launch_app.bat

Description of elements:
server.js - This is the backend support for the application, running express.js
index.html - This is the frontend for the application
global.json - Currently this exist just to manage the order of the maps in the application in the top menu
Maps - This folder houses the data supporting the application, it is dynamically managed by the app and holds images, text and canvas parameters.


Feature Explanation:
There is a top menu that allows the user to "Add Map" this will generate a folder for the map, this was designed with La-Mulana in mind which has numerous smaller maps.
Every generated map gets an entry in the top menu, when this entry is selected a canvas and notes section is generated for just that entry.
Right clicking a map entry lets you delete it, this does delete the entire folder.
The canvas allows dragging and dropping screenshots from the map which snap together, you can pan and zoom.
Right clicking an image allows you to give it a title (La-Mulana coded thought process here).
Each map entry has a note section tied to it in the right side of the application (look for the small pink line).

Note:
Speaking of the small pink line, I designed this with a color palette I find pleasing, changing the colors is very similar for anyone vaguely familiar with CSS.
If by some marvel people actually use this and there's an interest, I could easily add a configuration element to dynamically change the colors from the application.
